# Marketplace 66/66 execution plan

Plan of record for making all 66 unchanged titles of the EffectiveAcceleration `marketplace.test.ts` green on
mock BCH-2026, without Marketplace/Unicrow source changes and without application-specific logic.

- Rationale and evidence: [`EVAL_REMOVE_BATCH_ENTRYPOINT.md`](./EVAL_REMOVE_BATCH_ENTRYPOINT.md). Section
  references below (e.g. "EVAL 2.5") point there.
- How to use:
  - Tick `[x]` when a step is done and its evidence is recorded in the Log (section 7).
  - Untick a scoreboard title if it regresses.
  - Add a dated note instead of silently rewording a step.
- This file is the only copy. Do not copy it into branches; edit it here. If this worktree is ever removed, move
  the file first.

  - 2026-09-25 (review): decide on numbers. The relay limit is 100,000 B per transaction (policy) and the consensus
    limit 1,000,000 B (libauth). Every entry carries its own copy of the code, so code splitting bounds each master
    but not the transaction: `arbitrate`, about 24 masters, comes to roughly 120-240 KB (spec section 12). The
    largest titles would therefore be non-standard, though consensus-valid. A9 measures this (Phase R). Either way,

  - 2026-09-25 (follow-up): two layers. Per input, 10,000 B is consensus (libauth rejects longer unlocking bytecode
    before evaluation), so code splitting is required on a real chain. Per transaction, 100,000 B is only relay
    policy. So D3 asks "will these transactions relay, and what does submission cost", not "is this buildable". A9
    states both layers and the mitigations with their costs.

- **D6. Master and validator pool sizes** (spec section 12).
  - A transaction can enter a contract at most once per master it owns.
  - A composition consumes one validator of its root contract.
  - Options:
    - [x] A config default for composing contracts (e.g. 12 masters, 4 validators), overridable per contract and
      applied at deployment (recommended)
    - [ ] Deploy with 1 master and `split` in the harness before the suite
    - [ ] Other: ____
  - 2026-09-25, user decision: as many masters as needed. The measured worst case is Unicrow, entered 9 times in
    one `arbitrate` (spec section 21).
- **D7. `msg.sender` inside `this.g()`** (spec R3, T23, open point 9).
  - Either way, internal calls and top-level calls keep the calling user.
  - The marketplace is not affected: its sources and Unicrow contain no `this.f()` call.
  - Options:
    - [x] `address(this)`, as in Solidity; the spec is written this way (recommended)
    - [ ] The caller, as today's compiler does. Changes which account `this.transfer` / `this.approve` touch, and
      needs a sender-passthrough witness plus a validator check whenever the self-call cannot run inline
  - 2026-09-25, user decision: "msg.sender behavior should be identical to solidity". This covers every call
    context, not only `this.g()`. See `AUDIT_MSG_SENDER.md`.
- **D8. Call receipts** (spec R10, T32; audit S2).
  - Without receipts, one user signature authorizes any number of calls in the user's name. The calls sit in
    unlocking bytecode, which no signature covers.
  - Options:
    - [ ] A receipt output per user-rooted call, so the signature covers the exact list of calls (cost: one output
      per user-rooted call)
    - [x] No receipts for now. The risk is a documented residual (spec R10, T32). Receipts and the cheaper "one root
      per signed input" limit are written up as options in spec section 14.1
  - 2026-09-25, user decision: "no receipts for now, but document this option".
  - 2026-09-25 (review): T32 is an accepted residual.
    - Owner: the project owner.
    - Revisit before any real-chain deployment (D3), when transactions are assembled by third parties (relayers,
      batchers), or when wallets cannot decode the witnesses (spec open point 15).
    - Cost if adopted: the 66 make one user call per transaction, so one receipt output per transaction.
    - Adding receipts later does not need a new `V_TEMPLATE` if each receipt is an event the root master checks
      (spec 14.1).
    - The review recommends receipts on for user-rooted calls. That would reopen this decision; it is not adopted.
  - 2026-09-25 (follow-up): the revisit trigger splits by threat (spec 14.1).
    - Untrusted assembler (relayers, batchers): receipt events the root master checks are enough, and can be added
      later, per contract.
    - Hostile code in the call graph, with every call in the user's name attributable: only the validator-enforced
      form works. It is inside `V_TEMPLATE`, so its deadline is the freeze (D9), whether or not hostile code ever
      appears. It binds every root whose calls reach an honest contract (spec 14.1).
    - The 66 have neither (the SDK assembles every transaction), so the residual is inert here.
- **D9. Address model** (spec open point 13, T36; audit S12, F9).
  - An address must be bound on-chain to exactly one contract. Today's anchors are forgeable.
  - Options:
    - [x] Category-derived: the address of the contract's transcript (validator) contract,
      `addrV(cat) = P2SH32(pin(cat) || V_TEMPLATE)`, seeded with the same category pin as every other contract. The
      SDK reserves genesis outpoints when a CREATE address is predicted
    - [ ] Deployer-and-nonce addresses with deployer-signed anchors checked on-chain. Residual: a deployer can bind a
      second contract to their own address
  - 2026-09-25, user decision: "seed the transcript with category pin like other contracts do". Recorded as: an
    address is `addrV(cat)` (spec R5, R8, V11; open point 13).
  - 2026-09-25, user decision: version 1 does not allow validator program changes. The proxy-upgrade pattern covers
    upgradeable logic, and non-proxy contracts are immutable in Solidity. `V_TEMPLATE` v1 is frozen.
  - 2026-09-25 (review), recorded without changing the decision:
    - Proxies cover defects in contract logic, not in `V_TEMPLATE`. A proxy's own address and settlement use
      `V_TEMPLATE`, so a v1 defect stays with every v1 contract, proxied or not (spec section 9).
    - The freeze binds from the first real-chain deployment (D3), after an external audit (4.7). Until then a change
      to `V_TEMPLATE` only changes test addresses.
    - Open for the user before the freeze binds: keep this address form, or derive addresses from a tiny frozen
      dispatcher that carries the pin and routes to a versioned program (the review's recommendation). A dispatcher
      needs someone to authorize a new version; for a proxy that could be its admin.
  - 2026-09-25 (follow-up):
    - Precondition: no real-chain deployment before the address form is decided and the external audit covers that
      form (4.7). With a dispatcher, the audit covers two programs.
    - The validator-enforced receipts (D8) belong to the same pre-freeze decision, since they live in `V_TEMPLATE`.
    - Open for the user: when to decide. The follow-up review says before A8, because A4 and A7 freeze the address
      derivation there. Now it is a spec edit; after A8 it is a version bump every stream rebases onto; after a
      real-chain deployment it cannot change.
  - 2026-09-25, user decision: confirm `addrV(cat)` now, final for v1. No dispatcher. `V_TEMPLATE`'s content can still
    change until the freeze binds at the first real-chain deployment; each change only moves test addresses. The
    validator-enforced receipts (D8) therefore stay possible until then.

## 2. Conventions

### Worktrees

| Name | Path | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WT_NEW` | `/Code/cashscript/.worktrees/per-call` | All work from Phase 0 on, branch `feat/per-call` from `ea7a48e27`. Holds the plan documents in `docs/per-call/`. |
| `WT_CODEX` | `/Code/cashscript/.worktrees/kernel-beta-candidate` | Kernel work, ignored. Not frozen, fixed or measured. Its copies of these documents were deleted on 2026-09-25, after 0.2's commit. |
| `WT_CLEAN` | `/Code/cashscript/.worktrees/kernel-baseline-ea7a48e27` | Detached at `ea7a48e27`, built. Measurement reference for this plan; otherwise unused. |

### Commands (run from the worktree root)

They use the D2 harness, the root `vitest.marketplace.config.ts`.

```bash
# build (or keep `yarn build:watch` running)
yarn build

# fresh marketplace compile - REQUIRED after any compiler change: the project cache key excludes compiler code
rm -rf .marketplace/cache .marketplace/artifacts
node --max-old-space-size=8192 packages/testing/dist/cli.js compile --jobs 4

# fixture smoke test: title #15 runs only the fixture plus view calls
timeout 900 yarn vitest run --config vitest.marketplace.config.ts --no-file-parallelism \
  -t 'mece tags read mece tag$'

# single title: '<describe> <it>$' (7 titles are named "sanity checks", so always include the describe)
timeout 900 yarn vitest run --config vitest.marketplace.config.ts --no-file-parallelism \
  -t 'take job sanity checks$'

# full run (about 10 minutes when everything fails fast)
timeout 3000 yarn vitest run --config vitest.marketplace.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --reporter=verbose \
  > /tmp/marketplace-runs/$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)-$(date +%m%d-%H%M).log 2>&1   # mkdir -p /tmp/marketplace-runs first
```

A new worktree gets its own `node_modules`, never a symlink to another tree:
`yarn install --frozen-lockfile --offline --non-interactive` (about 2 minutes, including the postinstall `yarn build`).
Then verify that every `node_modules` is a real directory and every link inside resolves into the new tree:

```bash
W=$(pwd); find node_modules packages/*/node_modules examples/*/node_modules -type l |
  while read l; do case "$(readlink -f "$l")" in "$W"/*) ;; *) echo "OUTSIDE $l";; esac; done
```

Fallback if the offline cache misses a package: `cp -a` from `WT_CLEAN`, then the same check.

### Guardrails (apply to every step)

- One writer per worktree. Other agents work read-only or in their own worktree.
- Before recording any number, run the stability check: `git status --porcelain | sort | md5sum`, wait 45 s,
  repeat, and require both hashes to match.
- Record numbers only from committed states. Put the commit hash in the Log.
- Reviews of these documents target a commit hash, since the files change while they are being edited.
- Never `git add -A`: stage reviewed files only. Never `git stash`: the stash stack is shared across worktrees.
- Never edit Marketplace/Unicrow sources or the test file.
- No application-name logic. Gate on every diff:

  ```bash
  git diff -U0 -- packages/solidc/src packages/solidcash/src |
    rg '^\+.*(Marketplace|jobs\b|publishJobPost|publishJobEvent|JobEvent|Unicrow|FakeToken)'
  ```

- Every substantive fix gets a neutral regression test (no application names).
- The kernel worktrees and branches are ignored: no edits, fixes or freezes. The new path lives in `WT_NEW`.
- No `OP_RETURN` outputs and no new bare `OP_1` outputs. Where a placeholder is unavoidable, it is a 1,000-sat P2PKH to
  the transaction funder, and it is found by layout position, never by script (Track P rules, section 3a).

## 3a. Track P: placeholder outputs (`OP_RETURN` exclusion, `OP_1` revisit)

Every site is listed in [`PLACEHOLDER_OUTPUTS_INVENTORY.md`](./PLACEHOLDER_OUTPUTS_INVENTORY.md) (groups A-F, clean
HEAD `ea7a48e27`).

**Sequencing** (revised 2026-09-25):
- The new branch applies P0 (rules) and P4 (conformance).
- P1-P3 change the kernel path's existing code, which this goal now ignores. They are not scheduled. Their site
  lists stay in the inventory for reference, and Phase 3 removes most of those sites with the kernel.

### P0. Rules (effective now, for all code, including the new path)

- [x] Adopted: no `OP_RETURN` output in any transaction SolidCash builds. Not as a pad, not as a trailer or separator,
  and not as a data carrier: the transcript is never carried in `OP_RETURN` (spec R9 and section 14).
  - 2026-09-29: checked on the new path. The per-call subtrees (`packages/solidcash/src/per-call`,
    `packages/solidc/src/per-call`, `packages/utils/src/per-call`) build no `LockingBytecodeNullData` and no
    `0x6a` lock, and the hop the composer lays out carries none: the acceptance case is the "lays out the hop with
    no OP_RETURN and no bare OP_1 output" case of
    `packages/solidcash/test/per-call/call/proxy-call.test.ts`, which composes a whole hop through the shipped
    deployment, composer, derivation and machine and checks every output's lock.
- [x] Adopted: no new bare `OP_1` outputs.
  - 2026-09-29: same case: no output lock is the one-byte `0x51`, and no output has an empty lock or a
    non-positive value.
- [x] Adopted: where a placeholder output is unavoidable, it is a 1,000-sat P2PKH to the transaction funder (the fee
  payer, which is the change destination). No script counts a placeholder's value as contract value.
  - 2026-09-29: the new path lays out its participants by index and needs no placeholder, so the rule holds
    vacuously; the same case above is where a placeholder would show up as an output no participant claims.
- [x] Adopted: no code finds a placeholder by its script; it uses layout positions.
  - 2026-09-29: the new path builds no placeholder output to find. Its layout is positional
    (`packages/solidcash/src/per-call/composer/layout.ts`), and the per-call subtrees contain no script-pattern
    search for one.

## 4. Implementation: parallel workstreams

The spec fixes every interface the parts share: the witness block, the encodings, `M`, the record
formats, the frames and the V-checks. That makes an optimistic, parallel implementation possible, replacing the
earlier spike-then-rebuild sequence:
- after a short interface freeze (Wave 0), independent coders build separate code paths;
- each coder owns a focused test set under its own path;
- the full suite runs only at integration milestones.

The gate is kept, moved to milestone I2.

**Every implementation item below is one checkbox with its spec reference.** Tick it when the code lands and its
focused tests pass. This checklist is the only place implementation status is tracked.

A traceability check on 2026-09-25 found every item has a checkbox here:
- every spec check: spec P1-P2, W0-W3, O1, N1, spec S1-S4, V1-V11, and the spec's state rules D1-D2;
- every threat, T1-T41;
- every edge case (section 23, 26 rows);
- every Part II mechanism.

Items not needed for the 66 are in 4.7.

### 4.0 How the swarm runs

- **Streams and ownership.** Each stream owns its code directories and its test directory, and writes nowhere else.
  Shared files (`GenerateTargetTraversal.ts`, `compiler.ts`, SDK entry points) change only through small hook
  commits declared in advance.
- **Parallelism.**
  - At most 4 coders run at once (box capacity), in waves.
  - Each coder has one worktree and branch, off `feat/per-call`. The coordinator merges them into `feat/per-call`.
  - A coder's worktree is deleted right after its merge is verified.
- **Interfaces.** Frozen at the end of Wave 0, with golden vectors. A later change needs a version bump, updated
  vectors and the coordinator's approval; every stream then rebases.
- **Focused tests.**
  - A coder runs only their stream's directory, plus the shared vector tests (`yarn vitest run <dir>`).
  - `packages/solidcash/test/per-call/MANIFEST.md` lists every stream's directories and current pass counts. The
    coordinator updates it at each merge.
- **Full runs.**
  - `yarn test` runs only at milestones I2 and M2, and before the final merge.
  - The marketplace suite runs only from I3 on, at most once a day.
  - Flaky or shared-state tests are first confirmed with targeted runs.
- **Guardrails** (section 2) apply to every stream.
- **Names.** A bare label in this plan is a plan label.
  - Plan labels: decisions D1-D9; Track P items P0-P4; Track S items S0-S3; stream items A1-A8, B1-B15, C1-C14,
    R0-R7, E1-E13, F1-F7, G1-G6; milestones I1-I3, L1-L7, M1-M2; toys Y1-Y7 (renamed from T1-T7, so they do not
    clash with threats T1-T41).
  - Spec labels that could clash always carry "spec": spec P1-P2, spec S1-S4, spec R1-R10, and the spec's state
    rules D1-D2. Labels that exist only in the spec (W0-W3, O1, N1, V1-V11, T1-T41) need no prefix.
  - Shapes are in backticks (`A`, `ABBA`); streams are "stream A" and so on.
  - In the spec, bare D1-D2 are its state rules, and plan decisions are written "plan Dn".

| Stream | Owns (code) | Focused tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A Interfaces | `packages/utils/src/per-call/` | `packages/utils/test/per-call/` (with `vectors/`) |
| B Validator | `packages/solidc/src/per-call/validator/`, `packages/solidcash/src/per-call/validator/` | `packages/solidcash/test/per-call/validator/` |
| C Frames and calls | `packages/solidc/src/per-call/master/`, plus declared hooks | `packages/solidc/test/per-call/master/`, `packages/solidcash/test/per-call/frames/` |
| R Records (view mode) | `packages/solidc/src/per-call/records/`, plus declared hooks | `packages/solidc/test/per-call/records/` (codegen), `packages/solidcash/test/per-call/records/` |
| E Composer | `packages/solidcash/src/per-call/composer/` | `packages/solidcash/test/per-call/composer/` |
| F Deployment and proxies | `packages/solidcash/src/per-call/deploy/`, `packages/solidcash/src/per-call/proxy/` | `packages/solidcash/test/per-call/deploy/` |
| G Acceptance tests | Tests only | `packages/solidcash/test/per-call/{conformance,edges,hostile,toys,shapes}/` |

**Feasibility and dependencies** (assessed 2026-09-25):
- **Sequential first.** Stream A (interfaces), because every other stream codes against it.
- **Safe to run in parallel:**
  - B: stub masters, no compiler.
  - E: it starts on stub scripts that follow the A5 stop-site schema, then switches to real artifacts.
  - F: mostly SDK.
  - G: tests written test-first against the spec.
- **Parallel with care.** C and R both touch compiler codegen. Each lives in its own new module behind a declared
  hook. R is the critical path and the main risk: one coder, slices R1 to R7 in order.
- **Where optimism is tested:**
  - I1 (`ABBA`) needs A, B, C, R1-R2 and E;
  - I2 (the gate) also needs R3-R5 and F5-F6, for the proxy toy Y4;
  - I3 needs F7.
- **Where it fails, and the fallback.** If R's view mode needs changes all over `GenerateTargetTraversal.ts`, or the
  interfaces keep changing after A8 (every change forces rebases), cut back to fewer, sequential streams. The I2
  kill criteria catch the first case. Re-estimate for the fallback: about 8-12 weeks in total, as for spike then
  rebuild; record it in the Log when the fallback is taken.
- **Estimated timeline:**
  - Wave 0: 2-3 days.
  - Wave 1: about 2 weeks with 4 coders.
  - Wave 2 and I1-I3: 1-2 weeks.
  - Ladder: 1-2 weeks.
  - About 5-7 weeks in total, against 8-12 for spike then rebuild.

- [x] Every open point on the 66 critical path specified in spec Part II (since revision 9).
- [x] D6: as many masters as needed. Measured need: Unicrow 9 per transaction, and MarketplaceData 5 through its
  proxy and implementation.

### 4.2 Wave 1: core streams (B, C, R, E in parallel)

**Stream B: validator** (spec 3.2, 7.2). Its tests use hand-built transactions with stub masters (small scripts
holding minting NFTs, whose unlocking bytecode carries the A7 blocks), so B needs no compiler work.
- [x] B1 V1: recreation in place; a master of its own category present.
- [ ] B2 V2 (partial): parse `M` and every covered master's first-push witness block; reject any encoding the master
  would not accept. Emitted: the wire name and version, the root, master and settled-state indices, the witness-block
  shape and the empty settle tail. Not emitted: the remaining encoding rules.
- [x] B3 V3: completeness.
- [x] B4 V4: roots, and the forest rule.
- [ ] B5 V5 (partial): edges, for each kind. Emitted for an ordinary call: caller, kind, origin, value, sender,
  address, result, and the callee's own pushes hashed against the recorded digest; the `DELEGATE` target rule is
  emitted too (`fe87a8b22`: the target is the address of the callee master's own category). Not emitted: the
  `INTERNAL` same-contract rule, which the reference model checks (`V5_INTERNAL_CATEGORY_MISMATCH`). No compiled
  caller makes an `INTERNAL` call (4.7 defers them) and a callee's kind must match the record its caller computed,
  so no transaction carries such an edge until code-split contracts land.
  - `CALL`, `STATIC`, `CREATE`: sender is the caller's `self`, and `self` is the recorded target;
  - `DELEGATE`: passthrough, and the callee's category matches the target (T37);
  - `INTERNAL`: passthrough, same contract;
  - for all kinds: origin, values (passed through for `DELEGATE` and `INTERNAL`), `retval`, and `argsHash` over the
    callee's argument pushes.
- [x] B6 V6 (ticked 2026-09-28): every master visited exactly once, so cycles and unreachable masters are refused,
  and the ordering half is derived on chain: a recursive depth-first visit gathers each settled contract's record
  entries in the order the call tree gives, and the chains rule (B7) follows them in it, so a callee runs between
  its caller's segments and roots never interleave (T9, T30).
- [x] B7 V7 (ticked 2026-09-27; since 2026-09-28 the chains are followed in the V6 order rather than order-free, which
  retires the greedy walk and its refusals of branching chains, and the 400-case differential agrees): every settlement
  rule the program lists is held against the model over generated
  compositions and pinned by a machine refusal of its own — no category settled twice
  (`emitSettleCategoriesAreDistinct`),
  the state-inputs half (`emitSettlementStateInputs`: every input the transcript lists as a settled contract's state
  is a mutable NFT of its category and not the validator, every such input in the transaction is listed, and no index
  twice), the records the frames read against the state UTXOs the contract spends (`2cb452941`), the census
  (`d055ac85f`, `abe0de286`: no own-category fungible amount, a mutable own-category output only for a record a frame
  declares, a bare own-category output only for an event a frame lists inside the transaction and no event listed
  twice, and every master of the contract recreated at its own index), the value floor (`82879cfcc`) and the record
  chains (`ccde697cc`, this round for the end), both halves: an entry continues from the transaction's own commitment
  at the record's input or from another declaration's end view, and is continued by another declaration's start view
  or by the transaction's own commitment at the record's output, with a declaration that creates the record
  continuing from nothing and one that deletes it continued by nothing. The census reads
  `OP_OUTPUTTOKENCATEGORY` rather than the commitment because the opcode appends a capability byte only for mutable
  and minting tokens, so an immutable NFT of a settled category and a fungible token of it are the same 32 bytes on
  the wire (the Log row and Deviations carry the measurement). The chains are both halves: the pairing above, and the
  chain's end decided without the order by an anchor — every record entry carries a marker byte, one when the
  declaration's write lands at the transaction's own output or when it deletes the record, and an entry passes only
  if its key has a marked declaration anywhere in the blob. That is what puts `V7_CHAIN_END_MISMATCH` in the list, and
  the rule is checked both ways: with the anchor search neutered the differential misses `seed 24301 case 55` and
  with it the corpus is green. **Unticked again the same day: the pairing and the anchor are not connectivity.** Two
  read-only declarations of one record that both claim the same view pair with each other, and the record's honest
  write satisfies the anchor, so the program accepts a chain that never reaches the spent commitment; the model
  refuses it with `V7_CHAIN_BROKEN` (the Log row and the Deviations carry the repro and the rule the fix needs). Not
  in the program's list, and outside this item's scope: `V7_MASTER_NOT_COVERED` (carried by V3's master-set rule),
  `V7_RECORD_OUTPUT_NOT_A_RECORD` and `V7_SEND_OUTPUT_OUT_OF_RANGE`.
- [x] B8 V8: the settles set (two or more masters, or a `DELEGATE` or `INTERNAL` frame on the records). Both halves

- [x] B9 V9: owner policy.
- [x] B10 V10: static frames.
- [x] B11 V11: addresses, with `addrV` built from `OP_ACTIVEBYTECODE` (matches the A4 vectors).
- [x] B12 The `ABBA` golden transaction, with stub masters carrying the A7 blocks, is accepted. Verified

  - internal calls and `delegatecall` to own code, inline. Landed: an entry another body calls by name is inlined

  - `this.g()` inline with `msg.sender = self`, replacing the `AstBuilder.ts:7323` behaviour under per-call. Landed
    (`0e70219d6`): the caller hands the callee its own contract address as the callee's sender and address, so
    `msg.sender == address(this)` holds inside the self-called body and a caller-gated function reached that way is
    refused; the base-cast spelling agrees. `msg.value` inside a value-less self call is unchanged.
  - a runtime target equal to self as a `CALL`. Landed: a call through an interface value whose run-time target is
    the caller's own address (`IFoo(address(this)).m()`, `IFoo(this).m()`) is classified at its site as the value
    the caller's own code holds — its frame `self` — so the record's `target` is bound to it as it is for any
    computed target, and the callee runs on a second master of the same contract with `msg.sender == address(this)`,
    the same identity the inline `this.g()` presents. A target that is another contract is refused at the caller.
    The SDK's call path does not plan that callee's frame yet, so the conformance suite pins its row.

    row answers as the EVM's does.
- [x] C9 W3: events at their listed outputs; `sends[]` for P2PKH value sends; a value send to a contract as a `CALL`.
  Events by the census (`abe0de286`; T13, T41), P2PKH sends paid from the contract's containers (`5e671af32`;
  `hostile/send-list`, `hostile/send-output-binding`), and a payment to a contract as a `CALL` into its `receive()`
  (`9786657b4`; `hostile/contract-payment-plain-output`).
- [x] C10 Stop-site metadata emitted (A5). The per-call compiler derives each entry's sites from the calls it
  already compiles at their call sites and the segments they split the execution into — one `call` site per external
  call in execution order, then one `segmentClose` per segment, so `k` calls publish `2k + 1` sites — validates the
  table against the frozen schema before it is published, and attaches it to `artifact.composition`. The source-side
  facts a driver resolves a callee through (interface, method, target, selector) ride beside each call site, and no
  `read` site is published: the compiler does not hold the record identity a read resolves to, and an invented one
  would be worse than an omitted one.
- [x] C11 A code constant slot for `addrX`; stream F fills it at deployment.
- [x] C12 SafeERC20 low-level calls (OpenZeppelin 5.0.2 and 4.9.3) lowered to typed calls; the `code.length` rule.
  **Landed for the payloads the compiler can name** (`907cd7ed3`). A low-level call whose payload statically names
  an interface method — `address(t).call(abi.encodeCall(I.f, (args)))` or the `abi.encodeWithSelector(I.f.selector,
  args)` spelling, in the result-binding, result-ignoring and `return` positions — is rewritten before semantic
  analysis into the typed call `I(t).f(args)`, so the call record, the argument digest and the callee reference come
  from the same code path a written typed call uses; the low-level result is rebuilt as `success = true` and
  `returndata = abi.encode(<f's return values>)`, so `abi.decode(data, (bool))` round-trips. Measured: the derived
  call record matches the written typed call on every field and every contract input accepts
  (`edges/low-level-token-call-lowering.test.ts`). A payload held in a local and the vendored 4.9.3
  `Address.functionCall` indirection are lowered too (`693e8d441`, `e3eccbc7a`). **Refused by name**, by design: a
  run-time selector, an opaque `bytes` payload, `abi.encodeCall(this.f, ...)` and a method no known interface
  names. The `code.length` gate answers zero for a plain account or the zero
  address, as the EVM does for an account without code (log row "a target with no script answers empty code"), and a
  P2SH target answers its script when the transaction spends it.
  `address(this).balance` constant-folded for value 0 (spec 17; section 23 rows 9-11).
- [ ] C13 `ecrecover` returns address 0 for invalid input (spec 23 row 22). **Met on the per-call path for every
  argument the precompile refuses by range and for an `r` off the curve; open for a recovery at infinity**
  (`b382ff160` pinned it; `aac352885` and `a91a6c396` moved the per-call path from refusing every such body to serving
  it; log row "a recovery the precompile refuses answers the zero address"). The compiler emits a body that calls
  `ecrecover` and reads the co-spent pair at the master's own input plus `1 + 2i`/`2 + 2i`, and the composer places
  those inputs, builds them from the call's own argument pushes through the shipped witness and side-car builders,
  and shifts every later participant. No pair recovers from the arguments the precompile refuses, so the per-call
  body tests them itself: for a `v` outside 27/28, or an `r` or `s` outside [1, n), it answers the zero address,
  empty as `address(0)` is, without reading its pair, and the composer co-spends a placeholder pair there. An `r` in
  range but off the curve is served as well (log row "an r no curve point has answers the zero address"): side-car
  A's pad opens with w, whose square is -(r^3 + 7) mod p, and the body checks it before it answers the zero address.
  A recovery at infinity still sends the body to a pair none recovers; the direct convention has no zero-address
  rule. A recovery call whose argument the code computes is served
  (`101cb6131`), and so is a delegate frame's side-car placement; a loop over one stays open;
  `master/ecrecover-invalid-input.test.ts` pins each input shape beside a direct-path control.
- [x] C14 Fix: a public function that reads `msg.sender` and writes state fails `OP_VERIFY` when called internally
  (spec open point 9). Measured on the per-call path, where the scalar shape settles through `f()` and `this.f()`
  alike; the mapping shape, the spec's second finding, did not compile at all through `f()` and now settles (log
  row "an entry another body calls by name is inlined there, and a self-call keeps its own sender"). Through
  `this.f()` it stays refused: that is a message call (T23).
- [x] C15 Refusal is per body. A contract whose one function is a shape the master cannot serve still compiles: the
  bodies it can serve are emitted, the refused body is emitted as a body that fails whenever it is reached, and the
  fact that refuses it is published by name on `artifact.composition.refusedEntries`, so a builder reports which
  function is unsupported instead of the whole contract. The refusal closes over invocations, so an entry that runs
  a refused body is refused with it and named with the body it runs. Contract-wide stays contract-wide: a shape the
  head or the tail fixes (no entry point, a constructor the head cannot share, a fallback, contract creation,
  function pointers, inline assembly) refuses the unit rather than a body. A layout question is asked per body too: a
  body whose own layout places the dynamic-value chunk run at a width the head's one coordinate does not address is
  refused by name, and the master fixes the width most of its bodies use.

risk. Take the slices in order, each with its own tests.
- [x] R1 Data NFTs: reads from `viewIn`, and writes compared with `viewOut` at segment close, reusing today's record

  declared widths) and leaves the view of the record at the coordinate it is given, failing instead of falling back
  when a segment declares nothing there; a source read and the close both go through it; a value written before an
  external call is marked as the closed segment's so a read after the call resolves from the declaration; and the
  end-of-body rebuild closes each record against the segment the frame last touched it in. The worked shape where
  `A`'s one record is written by three frames now derives end to end and every contract input is accepted, with four
  controls refused (a frame whose computed commitment is not its segment's `viewOut`, one whose read is not its
  segment's `viewIn`, a standalone master whose last declaration is not the transaction's output, and a settlement
  whose later segment does not carry on from the one before it). Turning the declared read off fails seven of that
  file's ten cases and dropping the call-site marking fails five. Remaining: the close is emitted where the
  end-of-body rebuild runs, so a frame that writes a record early and leaves it untouched later does not prove that
  early value against that segment's declaration; a record whose index changes between segments is not followed; and
  dynamic chunks still resolve against the transaction.

  The gaps the emitted body still has are the ones R1's own text records (the close is emitted at the end-of-body

- [ ] R3 Mapping nodes:
  - exact read, and absence proof by predecessor;
  - update in place;
  - insert: a created record plus a relinked predecessor;

    lift `requireSatisfiableReachWrites` and `requireChainableNodes` for collections whose values do not chunk.

  coordinate (`__internal__dynamicChunkInputBase`) and nothing for the *value-witness* family: a

  any access that **reads** the node's value (a read-modify-write, or an array push into it, which is the
  marketplace's own `jobEvents[jobId].push`) needs the witness itself, and the **witness-block wire format has no
  variable-length value field**: supplying it takes either a wire-format change (version bump, validator V2,
  composer, machine) or materializing the value on chain from co-spent chunks, which the emitted body does not do.
  The composer is missing the other half — `planMappingWrite`/`layOutMappingWrites` place a node with a
  fixed-width tail, and the shipped chunk planner is for dynamic *state variables* while a long mapping value uses

  `valueChunkSignature`) that nothing lays out; the emitted body requires exactly `ceil(size/126)` value-chunk NFTs

  by name. **The delete half is served.** Codegen already lowered a sorted delete to an upsert of the value type's

    state in advance, so the hop is planned with a candidate and the value the entry actually computed is read
    back out of the machine - the entry closes its record against the declared view, the failed comparison leaves
    both operands, and the plan is rebuilt with the computed one (`deploy/declaration.ts`, shared with the
    genesis derivation). A frame's record-category check now resolves the *records' owner*: the executing input
    for a frame that owns its records, the caller's input for a delegate frame, which the witness block names as
    the caller reference. The head parks that index as one more tracked slot and the check reads it. Measured:
    the three-transaction deployment derives, every participant - both masters, the validator and the record - is
    accepted by the machine, and the record ends at the commitment the shipped encoder materializes from the
    written state with the implementation's address still in it, and a second `initialize` - offered the record the
    first one left, which is the `Initializable` flag set - is refused, with a control that the same plan offered the
    state the entry expects is accepted;
  - **a deviation is recorded for the record's shape**: a frame's write rebuilds the whole commitment from the
    fields *its own source* declares, so a proxy whose record does not declare the implementation's fields loses
    the address its fallback reads after the first call. A deployment therefore requires the two layouts to agree
    field by field and refuses a pair that does not (`39deb3656`, `records/partial-write.test.ts` measures the
    underlying property), and the proxy source declares the implementation's fields beside its own. The
    spec's section 19 wording ("its records hold the implementation's state layout plus one field") is realized
    this way; the built-in proxy of F5 is what removes the requirement by keeping the address in code;
  - **the SDK's ordinary entry point routes here** (`564d490e4`): `upgrades.deployProxy` reads the convention from
    the artifact's published descriptor and, for a per-call implementation, runs the same three transactions and
    returns the per-call deployment (`PerCallProxyDeployment`, not a `ProxyContract` - the doc comment and a branded
    overload say so). The proxy is the caller's or one generated from the implementation's declaration, and the
    options with no per-call equivalent (`initializer: false`, a non-Signer runner, a record-shaped seed) are
    refused with their own messages;
  - **the composer learns an unstated written view** (`3483fc768`): a plan may leave a segment's `viewOut` unstated,
    the draft replaces each unstated view with a placeholder, and a step that stops on one learns the value the body
    computed into it (the same channel the deployment layer reads). A stated view stays authoritative - a body that
    disagrees with it makes no progress and the stall is unchanged. A record whose output the plan leaves unstated
    carries the end of its declaration chain, recomputed each run, so a learned write reaches the output;
  - **the hop can be broadcast** (`a355347c3`): when the caller supplies its own funding, the derived hop is rebuilt
    on the outpoints the two geneses created - each participant found by enumerating its category rather than by
    assuming an index - with the assembled unlocking bytecodes and the derived outputs, the caller's own coin paying
    the fee and signing the transaction the root frame binds it to. One finding is recorded with it: the SDK's byte
    gate judges the hop against the production per-input limit and this composition's validator input is over it
    (10,567 against 10,000), which is what the composition profile exists for, so the hop goes to the provider's
    prepared-transaction path under that profile - on a real chain the per-call hop's input script is over the
    production limit whatever path builds it. The derived-only behaviour stays the default so callers that want the
    specification without sending it keep working.
- [x] (with F6) The validator program binds a delegate call's target to the callee's own code (`fe87a8b22`): the
  reference checker and the reason list named `V5_DELEGATE_TARGET_MISMATCH` but the shipped program did not emit
  it, so the machine accepted a delegate callee that was not the contract the caller's record named. The
  program-versus-derivation differential run keeps both directions clean.

  deployed ones.

      run-time argument settles and MS2's replica dropped the forwarding spelling. **P17 is served as of
      2026-09-28** (`693e8d441`): a payload at the call site, in a local, and through a helper's parameter - the
      `Address.functionCall` indirection - all lower to the typed call they denote, and a payload the compiler
      cannot name still refuses by name. P19: long values in chunks, partial (R5).
    - **Where the shapes stand, measured 2026-09-28 by compiling the project and reading every artifact's
      `composition.refusedEntries`** (78 refusals across the seven contracts when the census was first taken, by
      the reason the compiler publishes; **31** after the initializer inference stopped injecting the direct
      convention's proxy operand, **23** after the round that served the chunk-run and key shapes, and **13** after
      the round that served a call the source does not fix and a mapping write a call precedes):
      **52** of the original 78 were a proxy implementation's own entry, refused for the hidden
      `__internal__proxyMasterIndex` operand
      that Solidity-compatible initializer inference injects and a per-call delegate frame never reads
      (`MarketplaceDataV1` 37, `MarketplaceV1` 15 - the two roots that MS2, MS3, MS4, MS5 and MS8 all stand on);
      **16** were a body that reads or writes a dynamic value *beside* an external call, where the value's chunk run
      and the call's blocks share the frame's records (`MarketplaceV1`, mostly the job-post writers MS2 and MS5
      need); **3** were a
      dynamic-value chunk run whose width differs from the one coordinate the master leaves its bodies
      (`MarketplaceDataV1`'s two address-array getters and `FakeToken.__construct`); and **1** was a mapping write
      whose key is a ternary over values the body holds or a field of the state record rather than a bare parameter,
      the frame's sender or a compile-time value (`MarketplaceV1.refund`, `MarketplaceV1.refuseArbitration`,
      `Unicrow.pay` - MS3's pull). All of those are served now, along with the fifteen that were a call running
      conditionally, where the paths through the entry did not make the same number of calls. What the **12** that
      remain are, largest wall first:
      **8** are the raw low-level spelling of a call, which takes the direct path's return-event or value-transfer
      machinery that a per-call body does not emit (`MarketplaceV1`'s job-post writers, its releases and
      `payStartJob` - MS2's and MS5's own writers, so this is the wall those two replicas stand on - and
      `Unicrow.refund`/`sendEscrowShare`, whose send half is served and whose value-carrying low-level call is what
      refuses); **2** are a verified-mapping write behind a call whose occurrence the source does not fix, so the
      derived operands cannot follow the segment the write lands in (an imported token's `transferFrom`, and
      `Unicrow.pay` - MS3's pull); **1** is a keccak compute side-car whose
      co-spent inputs the master head does not locate (`MarketplaceV1.takeJob`); and **1** is a derived write key
      that reads an element of a dynamic state array (`MarketplaceV1.refuseArbitration`), which the derivation
      cannot emit where it runs. The send wall is gone: a listed send's lock may be a value the body computes, the
      body pins the lock and value it computed at the listed output, and a position the execution did not send at
      must carry the sentinel.
      The order the shapes take follows those counts, largest wall first.
      **Admission is gated on the T44 class** (the parallel worker's safety gate, 2026-09-28): no further shape is
      accepted until every record a frame declares in a segment is either checked against the code that declares it
      or required unchanged, and the shapes accepted after `6dd0bdfd8` — whose record positions move with the calls
      an execution actually made — are to be brought under that rule rather than exempted from it.

### 4.6 Rules

- [ ] **Order before the ladder** (the user's I2b decision, made operational on 2026-09-27; superseded by the
  fixture-first rule below on 2026-09-28, which is what rounds follow until the fixture title is green):
  - a round takes the first unticked item of I1, then I2 (Y1-Y7, G5, G3), then I2b (MS1-MS10), and its Log row names
    that item and the `MARKETPLACE_SHAPES.md` row it moved;
  - the marketplace project is compiled at most once per milestone, to refresh the catalog; no title and no fixture
    runs, and a Log row carries no ladder paragraph;
  - a toy or replica settles in its own shape. A narrower variant (a loop for separate call statements, a scalar
    rewrite for an array append, fewer turns, no events) is logged as partial and leaves the toy's box and the
    catalog row's status unchanged.
- [x] **M1 is claimed only with strict matchers** (coordinator direction 2026-09-30). The harness's
  `revertedWith` accepted any thrown failure outside three construction-message patterns and `withArgs` did not
  compare arguments at all, so a revert or rejection title could pass because the call failed for an unrelated
  reason -- six of the seventeen green titles are exactly that kind, and this is the weakness that made an earlier
  "66/66" claim misleading. For a per-call contract the matchers compare the entry's own reason and its error
  arguments; a failure the harness produced does not satisfy a contract-reason expectation; and a matcher that
  cannot observe the arguments refuses loudly rather than passing. The count is expected to **drop** when this
  lands, and the M1 (>=45/66) claim waits for it.
- [x] **No repeated-byte identifiers in tests** (user direction 2026-09-30). A 32-byte constant whose bytes all
  repeat -- `'66'.repeat(32)`, `'11'.repeat(32)` -- is its own reverse, so a byte-order mistake in the code or in the
  VM cannot show up as a mismatch, and a category that reverses to itself hides exactly the class of bug the tests
  exist to catch. Every category, txid and outpoint a test names uses bytes that are neither constant nor
  palindromic, and where a value's byte order matters the two orders differ. Agents are told the same in every
  brief. A sweep of the existing focused tests replaces the repeated constants; a test that compares a derived
  value to such a constant keeps working because the constant changes on both sides.
- [x] **Targeted title runs, not full ladders** (user direction 2026-09-30). A round does not run the
  66-title ladder for its own sake: it runs the one failing title it is fixing, and when that title turns green it
  runs the title that precedes it in the file as a regression check. The full ladder is reserved for a milestone
  (M1/M2), for an explicit request, or for a change so broad that no single title stands for the others -- and
  then its per-test and full-run times are recorded as before. A targeted run pays the fixture's own deployment
  either way (about 350 s), so the two runs are what a round costs, not the fifty-minute ladder. The last full
  ladder on record is run 16 (17/66, 3219.1 s); its wall and times are in section 4.5 and the Log.
- [x] **Fixture-first while the roots are compiler-bound** (coordinator decision, 2026-09-28; the order returns to
  I2b with the fixture parked at its measured wall - see the note at the end of this bullet). Rounds took the next
  wall the real project reported - the project compile's first failure, then the fixture's own - ahead of the
  unlanded per-shape replicas, and it earned its place: three real defects (the multi-entry value slot, the reserved
  slot anchored on a body constant, the head's call count against refused entries) came out of compiling the real

  - Measured on the reference composition at the published density before and after the program's padding block:
    the budget is 800 operation-cost units per byte of the validator input's own unlocking bytecode, and the shipped
    program spent 3,142,116 of the 3,812,000 those bytes buy — 17% of headroom — and 3,810,464 of 3,810,400 on the
    emitting round trip's shape, 64 over, so that transaction was unspendable while the validator's own derivation
    accepted all eleven checks. The program now carries a block of inert bytes it pushes and drops where it ends
    (`7c76dcef4`): 3,201,534 of 5,452,000, 41% of headroom, for 28,698 extra bytes pushed. The padding is a fixed
    block, so what still comes before a larger shape is the bytes that make it up: a composition whose own program
    and transcript approach the ten-thousand-byte limit on an unlocking bytecode needs a leaner walk — each covered
    master's unlocking bytecode read once rather than once per check, since the reads are what the pushed bytes are.

## 5. Phase 3: delete and consolidate (after M2)

- [ ] Remove route synthesis (`__message_bus1`, `SCB1`), the row loop, and the `__internal__graph*` bands.
- [ ] Remove static footprint recipes: permutations, cursors, access programs, constructed-key replay,
  loop-domain proofs.
- [ ] Remove the per-shape logic in the layout resolver and the worklist.
- [ ] Reduce the admission catalog to `KERNEL_OPAQUE_EFFECT` and `KERNEL_FOREIGN_DELEGATE`.
- [ ] Retire or re-scope `messageBus`, `messageBusKernel` and `messageBusGraphContext`.
- [ ] Replace `scripts/kernel-beta-manifest.json` with a proof set for the new composition path.
- [ ] Track P4: delete the remaining group C/D machinery, i.e. the `P2SH32(OP_TRUE)` dummy funders and the
  `provider.addUtxo` minting (inventory).
- [ ] Full `yarn test` and `yarn build` green. Docs updated: `message-bus-kernel.md`, `call-model.md`,
  `auto-derivation.md`.

### Phase R: real-chain deployment (after M2, per D3)

- [ ] A9 Size budget, the first step. Owner: the coordinator; about 1 day; its result gives Phase R's estimate.
  Bytes per transaction for `arbitrate` and `approveResult`: masters x (code + witness + arguments + views), plus
  the validator with density padding, state inputs and outputs, from the per-call artifacts' per-function code
  sizes. The recorded result (Log) must state:
  - both layers, with numbers: per input, 10,000 B consensus (code splitting required); per transaction,
    100,000 B relay policy and 1,000,000 B consensus;
  - first, the loader (spec 12, mitigation 1): one copy per distinct code instead of per entry; each master's
    executed-instruction count against its budget of 8 instructions per unlocking byte; the padding needed; and the
    total against 100,000 B;
  - then the other mitigations with their costs: smaller facets (linear at best); direct submission to miners (an
    operational dependency); fewer entries per transaction (gives up atomicity, the design's premise).
- [ ] The validator spans several inputs (spec section 24; user decision 2026-09-28): a head at `addrV(cat)` and
  `K - 1` facets at `head + k`, each running its share of the checks on its own operation-cost budget, the head
  binding each facet's lock and in-place recreation, each facet reading `M` from `OP_INPUTINDEX - k`. A9 sizes `K`
  and the split from the measured program (10,270 B, input 10,354 B at the order walk) and from `arbitrate`; the
  facet hashes join `V_TEMPLATE` before the freeze binds (open point 13). Hostile cases: a facet left out, moved,
  of other code, or reading another head's transcript.
- [ ] The precondition in 4.7 holds before any real-chain deployment.
- [ ] A separate harness at real limits: 10,000 B per input, 800 op-cost per byte, 128 B commitments, 100 KB relay.
  It starts from the published-density measurements (4.6, "Limit profile for the gates"), which become its gate.
- [ ] Facet-split the large handlers: the 75 KB entry closure, and the 90-200 KB contracts.
